data.long_meaning: Adonijah (אֲדֹנִיָּה) is a name of Hebrew origin meaning “My Lord is Yah (the Lord)”. A theophoric compound of Hebrew אָדוֹן (ʾadon) 'lord, master' (with possessive yod) and יָהּ (Yah), the shortened divine name - 'my Lord is Yah'. Its root is Hebrew אֲדֹנִיָּה (ʾAdoniyyah), from אָדוֹן (ʾadon) 'lord' + יָהּ (Yah), the shortened divine name. Adonijah is the anglicised form of Biblical Hebrew ʾAdoniyyah.

Its root is Hebrew אֲדֹנִיָּה (ʾAdoniyyah), from אָדוֹן (ʾadon) 'lord' + יָהּ (Yah), the shortened divine name. Adonijah is the anglicised form of Biblical Hebrew ʾAdoniyyah.

faq.a: The root of Adonijah is Hebrew אֲדֹנִיָּה (ʾAdoniyyah), from אָדוֹן (ʾadon) 'lord' + יָהּ (Yah), the shortened divine name.

faq.q: What is the etymology of Adonijah?
faq.a: A theophoric compound of Hebrew אָדוֹן (ʾadon) 'lord, master' (with possessive yod) and יָהּ (Yah), the shortened divine name - 'my Lord is Yah'.

faq.q: Does Adonijah appear in the Bible?
faq.a: Yes. The personal name occurs in the Hebrew Bible (2 Samuel 3:4; 1 Kings 1-2).

faq.q: Is Adonijah a Biblical name?
faq.a: Yes — the personal name occurs in the Biblical text. The personal name occurs in the Hebrew Bible (2 Samuel 3:4; 1 Kings 1-2).

faq.q: Does Adonijah occur in the Old Testament?
faq.a: Yes.

faq.q: Does Adonijah occur in the New Testament?
faq.a: No — it is not attested in the New Testament.

faq.q: Is Adonijah associated with a saint?
faq.a: No saint association is verified for the name Adonijah.

faq.q: Is the meaning of Adonijah verified?
faq.a: The meaning “My Lord is Yah (the Lord)” is supported by Old Testament: a son of King David who attempted to seize the throne (1 Kings 1-2). Confidence: HIGH.

faq.q: What is the numerology or lucky number of Adonijah?
faq.a: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Adonijah total 62, reducing to 8. Number 8 is traditionally associated with ambition, authority and material success. This is an interpretive tradition, not a factual claim.

faq.q: What are the common spelling variants of Adonijah?
faq.a: Variants and alternative forms include Adoniyah, Adoniah, Adonias.

faq.q: What is the transliteration of Adonijah?
faq.a: Adonijah is transliterated as ʾAdoniyyah.

faq.q: How many syllables does Adonijah have?
faq.a: Adonijah has 4 syllables.

faq.q: What are the spiritual connotations of Adonijah?
faq.a: Any spiritual significance attached to Adonijah is interpretive. Its documented core is the lexical meaning “My Lord is Yah (the Lord)”, and readings built on that meaning are presented as tradition rather than as religious doctrine.

faq.q: Where is the name Adonijah used today?
faq.a: Adonijah circulates chiefly in Biblical Hebrew, English, Greek, Latin naming communities. No verified registration statistics are published for it.
